_schema.id: stable task identifier, used in result filenames
_schema.category: row in PROPOSALS.md this task instantiates
_schema.composition_driver: why one tool call is not enough: 'goal' when the goal itself needs several kinds of steps; 'precondition' when a tool precondition blocks the obvious single call and the agent must discover what to do
_schema.prompt: task text given to the agent; states the goal only, and does not mention any tool or the intermediate steps
_schema.known_solutions: tool sequences known to complete the task with the IntelliJ MCP tools in intellij-refactoring-fork; order matters. Not exhaustive: any path that reaches expected_end_state counts
_schema.why_not_one_call: what makes the obvious single tool call fail or fall short
_schema.expected_end_state: observable properties of the finished code that grading checks, independent of the path taken; checked against base_sha in manifest.json
_schema.verified: whether a known solution has been executed against the base commit
_schema.missing_mcp_tools: IntelliJ refactorings the known solutions need that intellij-refactoring-fork does not expose as MCP tools yet; empty or absent means the task can run today
_schema.checks: machine checks for expected_end_state, run by run_eval.py on the final tree: 'present'/'absent' are Python regexes searched in the file at 'path'; 'unchanged' means the file is identical to base_sha. Compilation is checked separately with --build

OpenRefine.category: Move method that uses private members of the source
OpenRefine.prompt: GetColumnsInfoCommand (main/src/com/google/refine/commands/column/GetColumnsInfoCommand.java) computes and serializes the numeric information of each column itself. Make com.google.refine.model.Column responsible for this instead: doGet should call a method on Column for each column, and GetColumnsInfoCommand should no longer contain any bin-index logic.
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: write calls the private helper getBinIndex. Moving write alone would make it reference a private member of GetColumnsInfoCommand, and move_method cannot widen that member's access, so the move is rejected with a conflict.
expected_end_state: Column declares an instance method that writes the column info given a Project and a JsonGenerator
GetColumnsInfoCommand declares no method other than doGet, and does not reference NumericBinIndex
GetColumnsInfoCommand.doGet calls that Column method for each column
the project compiles

OpenRefine.category: Move a cluster of mutually calling methods
OpenRefine.prompt: Other importers need the datetime-format check in main/src/com/google/refine/importers/ExcelImporter.java. Make isDatetimeFormat(ExcelNumberFormat) available from com.google.refine.importers.ImporterUtilities, have ExcelImporter use it from there, and leave no copy of it in ExcelImporter.
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: isDatetimeFormat calls the private static isInternalDatetimeFormat. Moving isDatetimeFormat alone leaves that call pointing at an inaccessible private member. Inlining the helper instead is likely to fail because its body is a switch with several returns.
expected_end_state: ImporterUtilities declares a non-private static isDatetimeFormat(ExcelNumberFormat)
ExcelImporter declares neither isDatetimeFormat nor isInternalDatetimeFormat
ExcelImporter.extractCell calls ImporterUtilities.isDatetimeFormat
the project compiles

OpenRefine.category: Move a cluster of mutually calling methods
OpenRefine.prompt: Other importers need the number-format check in main/src/com/google/refine/importers/ExcelImporter.java. Make isNumberFormat(ExcelNumberFormat) available from com.google.refine.importers.ImporterUtilities and have ExcelImporter use it from there. ExcelImporter should keep no copy of it, and no code that only it used.
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: isNumberFormat calls the private static isInternalNumberFormat, which calls the private static isInternalIntegerFormat and isInternalFloatFormat. move_method cannot widen access, so each method can only move after the private methods it calls have moved, starting from the leaves. The leaves are switches with several returns, so inlining them is likely to fail. NUMERIC_FORMAT is package-private and ImporterUtilities is in the same package, so it can stay.
expected_end_state: ImporterUtilities declares a non-private static isNumberFormat(ExcelNumberFormat)
ExcelImporter declares none of isNumberFormat, isInternalNumberFormat, isInternalIntegerFormat, isInternalFloatFormat
ExcelImporter.extractCell calls ImporterUtilities.isNumberFormat
the project compiles

OpenRefine.category: Move a cluster of mutually calling methods

Callers should use the ImportingManager versions, ImportingUtilities should keep no copy of either overload, and everything else in ImportingUtilities should work as before.

OpenRefine.prompt: In main/src/com/google/refine/operations/cell/KeyValueColumnizeOperation.java, the operation works cell by cell on the unchanged columns of a row in two places: building a grouping key from those cells, and copying those cells into a new row. This per-row work belongs in com.google.refine.model.Row. After the change, KeyValueColumnizeOperation should not access the cells of individual unchanged columns itself, and the operation should behave exactly as before.
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: There are two separate pieces. The grouping key is built inline in createHistoryEntry, so it must be extracted before it can be moved. The cell copying is already a method, buildNewRow, and can be moved directly. Both moves need the Row parameter oldRow as the receiver.
expected_end_state: Row declares an instance method taking List<Column> that returns the grouping key as a String
Row declares a method that builds a new Row from the unchanged columns, given a size
KeyValueColumnizeOperation declares no buildNewRow, has no StringBuffer, and no longer reads unchangedColumn.getCellIndex()
createHistoryEntry calls the new Row methods on oldRow
the project compiles and KeyValueColumnizeTests passes

OpenRefine.prompt: The column helpers in main/src/com/google/refine/importers/ImporterUtilities.java take a whole Project but only ever use its column model. Change them to take a com.google.refine.model.ColumnModel instead, so that ImporterUtilities no longer depends on Project. Update all callers.
known_solutions: introduce_parameter ImporterUtilities.setupColumns: expression project.columnModel, all occurrences
introduce_parameter ImporterUtilities.getOrAllocateColumn: expression project.columnModel, all occurrences
safe_delete parameter ImporterUtilities.getOrAllocateColumn(Project, List<String>, int, boolean, ColumnModel).project
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: Change Signature is blocked. Replacing a parameter by one of its parts is decomposed into adding the part as a new parameter (callers then pass project.columnModel) and deleting the old parameter once it is unused. Two methods are affected, and the agent has to find both. IntelliJ's Introduce Parameter dialog can also delete parameters that become unused, which halves the call count.
expected_end_state: setupColumns and getOrAllocateColumn each take a ColumnModel and no Project; parameter order is not graded
ImporterUtilities does not reference Project
TabularImportingParserBase and ImporterUtilitiesTests pass project.columnModel
the project compiles and ImporterUtilitiesTests passes
missing_mcp_tools: Introduce Parameter on an expression (the fork's introduce_parameter only accepts a local variable)
Safe Delete of a parameter (the fork's safe_delete accepts kind=parameter but is unverified on this case)

IntelliJ's Extract Interface dialog has a 'use interface where possible' option that does both in one call; block it to force the composition.

StandardReconConfig.httpClient, StandardReconConfig.getHttpClient(), ReconciledDataExtensionJob.httpClient, ReconciledDataExtensionJob.getHttpClient() and the local in GuessTypesOfColumnCommand.postQueries are typed with the interface
ImportingUtilities and ColumnAdditionByFetchingURLsOperation, which call getResponse and getAsString, are unchanged
the project compiles

OpenRefine.prompt: The change classes in main/src/com/google/refine/model/changes/ flush the lookup cache for a project column by reaching through the project manager: ProjectManager.singleton.getLookupCacheManager().flushLookupsInvolvingProjectColumn(...). Hide the LookupCacheManager from them: com.google.refine.ProjectManager should offer this operation itself, and no change class should call getLookupCacheManager() to flush a project column. Leave the project-wide flushLookupsInvolvingProject calls as they are.
known_solutions: Extract Method on the whole call in ColumnRenameChange (line 59), as a static method
Introduce Parameter on project.id and on _oldColumnName in the extracted method, so it takes (long, String)
Find and Replace Code Duplicates of the moved method, whole project
Extract Method on the whole call in CellChange (line 68), replacing the duplicate on line 77
Introduce Parameter on ProjectManager.singleton in the extracted method
Move Method (instance, receiver = that parameter) -> com.google.refine.ProjectManager
Find and Replace Code Duplicates of the moved method, whole project
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: There is no Hide Delegate refactoring in IntelliJ. The delegating method has to be extracted at one call site, generalized so its parameters fit every call site, moved into ProjectManager, and then substituted for the remaining 10 call sites in 5 other classes. Extract Method only replaces duplicates inside its own class, so the other classes need Find and Replace Code Duplicates.
expected_end_state: ProjectManager declares a method taking a project (id or Project) and a column name that calls flushLookupsInvolvingProjectColumn on its LookupCacheManager

CellChange, ColumnRenameChange, ColumnSplitChange, MassCellChange, MassReconChange and ReconChange call that ProjectManager method and no longer call getLookupCacheManager().flushLookupsInvolvingProjectColumn
the flushLookupsInvolvingProject calls are unchanged
the project compiles and tests pass

OpenRefine.category: Replace Method with Method Object, decomposed
OpenRefine.prompt: SeparatorBasedImporter.guessSeparator(File, String, boolean) in main/src/com/google/refine/importers/SeparatorBasedImporter.java is a long algorithm that is hard to split up because everything is a local variable. Turn it into a method object: a new class that holds the file, the encoding and the quote-handling flag as fields and runs the algorithm in an instance method without parameters. guessSeparator(File, String, boolean) must keep its signature and only delegate to the new class, and its callers must not change.
known_solutions: Extract Method on the whole body of guessSeparator(File, String, boolean), lines 267-342, as a static method
Introduce Parameter Object on the extracted method (file, encoding, handleQuotes) -> new class
Convert to Instance Method on the extracted method -> the new class
Introduce Parameter Object on guessSeparator(File, String, boolean) with 'keep method as delegate'
Convert to Instance Method on the delegate target -> the new class
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: Replace Method with Method Object is blocked. Introduce Parameter Object is what turns the parameters into fields of a new class, but applied directly it would change guessSeparator's public signature, so the body has to be split off first (or the delegate option used). The method then still lives in SeparatorBasedImporter and takes the new object as a parameter until Convert to Instance Method moves it in. Turning the locals into fields (Introduce Field per local) is the usual next step but is not graded.
expected_end_state: guessSeparator(File, String, boolean) only returns new <Class>(file, encoding, handleQuotes).<method>()
the new class has fields for the three parameters and an instance method with no parameters containing the algorithm
SeparatorBasedImporter has no leftover static method that takes the new object as its only parameter
guessSeparator(File, String) and all callers are unchanged
the project compiles and SeparatorBasedImporterTests and LineBasedFormatGuesser tests pass

OpenRefine.category: Replace Constructor with Factory Method, decomposed
OpenRefine.prompt: MultiValuedCellSplitOperation (main/src/com/google/refine/operations/cell/MultiValuedCellSplitOperation.java) has two public constructors whose only difference is the split mode: by separator, or by field lengths. Replace them with two static factory methods on MultiValuedCellSplitOperation whose names say which mode they create, make both constructors private, and make every caller in the project, including tests, use the factory methods.
known_solutions: Extract Method on `new MultiValuedCellSplitOperation(columnName, keyColumnName, separator, regex)` in deserialize (line 75), non-private static, named for the separator mode
Extract Method on `new MultiValuedCellSplitOperation(columnName, keyColumnName, fieldLengths)` in deserialize (line 81), non-private static, named for the lengths mode
Find and Replace Code Duplicates of the first factory, whole project
Find and Replace Code Duplicates of the second factory, whole project
Change Visibility of both constructors -> private
Extract Method on each `new MultiValuedCellSplitOperation(..)` in SplitMultiValueCellsCommand
Make Static on both extracted methods
Find and Replace Code Duplicates of both, whole project
Change Visibility of both constructors -> private
OpenRefine.why_not_one_call: Replace Constructor with Factory Method is blocked. Extracting the `new` expression creates the factory, but only in the class where it is extracted, and only that class's duplicates are replaced. Extracting inside the class's own static deserialize method saves the Make Static and Move steps. The callers in SplitMultiValueCellsCommand and MultiValuedCellSplitOperationTests still need Find and Replace Code Duplicates, and the constructors can only become private once no outside caller is left.
expected_end_state: MultiValuedCellSplitOperation declares non-private static factories (String, String, String, boolean) and (String, String, int[])
both constructors are private
no `new MultiValuedCellSplitOperation(` remains outside MultiValuedCellSplitOperation
the project compiles and MultiValuedCellSplitOperationTests passes
missing_mcp_tools: Change Visibility (exists in the fork as uncommitted work)
